The student has computed the first four terms of the sequence correctly according to the recurrence relation. They then observe that the sequence "appears to be increasing and bounded above by 2." This is an empirical observation based on numerical approximations, not a rigorous proof. In Real Analysis, we cannot rely on numerical approximations or visual appearances to establish monotonicity and boundedness; we must provide a deductive argument using inequalities and induction. While the observation might guide intuition, it does not constitute a valid proof step. The student needs to formally prove monotonicity (e.g., by showing \(a_{n+1} \ge a_n\) ∀ \(n\)) and boundedness (e.g., by showing \(a_n \le 2\) ∀ \(n\)) using algebraic manipulation and induction.
